text: The M-94, the US Army's cipher cylinder until 1942, is 25 discs with published mixed alphabets: set the message along one row, copy out another. Only the disc order and the row were secret.

Each known letter allows only the discs that carry the carved letter the right number of places after it; the discs at different places must all be different. Every group start and every row choice, decided exactly; ten scrambled copies, two planted texts.
No disc order fits K4 or any copy under any setting; planted texts are found. F11.1 closed for the M-94.
